subject: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finservco.com>, Aaron Chu <aaron.chu@finservco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement

Hi Lena / Aaron — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap & proposed next steps so we’re aligned internally and with your team. Notes pulled from our call (short):

- Primary objectives: reduce inference spend by ~30% on batch jobs, and cut tail-latency for customer-facing features to <120ms p95.
- Key stakeholders we heard:
  - Economic buyer: Aaron Chu (Finance) — cares about TCO, contract length, and committed spend forecast.
  - Technical eval: Lena Ortiz (AI Platform) — performance, latency, and integration effort.
  - Security & procurement: procurement@finservco.com (procurement team) + legal (TBD).
- Constraints called out: SOC 2 evidence, data residency (US-only), and a procurement template requiring standard SLAs and indemnities.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
1) Align internal champion enablement: I’ll send a 10–15 minute "ally kit" for Lena to use with Aaron (ROI bullets, one-pager, 2-slide economic summary). Attaching early drafts.
2) Security checklist: Neha, can you review the questionnaire (attached) and flag any gaps we should pre-fill?
3) Procurement path: Jordan to coordinate a short call between Aaron and our Sales Ops to discuss committed capacity options and an estimate. Procurement team asked for a mutual action plan — attached draft.
4) Technical follow-up: Rishi to provide expected deployment footprint, network requirements, and 95/99 latency numbers for the referenced model.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 10/20: 30-min alignment with Lena to walk the ROI and ask list (Lena prefers mornings).
- Wed 10/21: Security Q&A draft sent to procurement.
- Fri 10/23: Sync w/ Aaron (economic buyer) + quick pricing sketch.

Please confirm availability or suggest changes. Lena — if you prefer to demo a quick sandbox instead of the ROI call, we can switch the Tue slot to a 20-min environment walkthrough.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (555) 214-0097

Attachments: FinServCo_ROI_one_pager.pdf (1 page), FinServCo_Sec_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (xlsx), Mutual_Action_Plan_FinServCo.docx (docx)

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Chu <aaron.chu@finservco.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. I skimmed the ROI one-pager and it hits most of what I need. A couple small asks from me:

- Can you add a short line showing expected latency improvement for our 1k qps peak (p50/p95 numbers)? That helps me in the platform team review.
- For procurement, we’ll need the SLA language and a sample data processing addendum (DPA) — can you point me to those?

I’m happy to be the internal ally and run a 20–30 minute alignment with Aaron next Tue morning (10/20) at 9:30am PT, if that works. If you want Rishi there for technical backup, include him.

Lena Ortiz
Senior Engineer, AI Platform
FinServCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement

Nice recap, Jordan. A few tactical notes from me:

- Aaron is the economic buyer, make sure any committed capacity options show 12/24/36 month scenarios and an ARR impact line. He tends to prefer clear, conservative uplift numbers.
- For the ally kit: include a one-line "ask" for the champion to send to the buyer (e.g., "Request a single 30-min meeting with finance to review pricing for committed capacity"). Executable language helps.
- Rishi: please include a short bullet on expected uplift vs their current LLM infra (examples: token cost reduction %, ops headcount delta).

I’ll review the MAP doc and propose language for the procurement timeline. Jordan — loop me in on the Tue 9:30am PT slot and I’ll join if Aaron wants to escalate.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finservco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement

Lena / Jordan — quick technical notes I can bring into the Tue alignment:

- Expected p50/p95 for your 1k qps (approx): p50 ~ 35ms, p95 ~ 110ms for the quantized model on c5-gpu-style fleet with prefix caching.
- Footprint estimate: 4 dedicated GPUs for peak 1k qps (with autoscale headroom), 16GB KV cache per node recommended.
- Network & integration: needs standard HTTPS with mutual TLS optional; no inbound VPN required.
- Risk notes: we will need to confirm whether FinServCo requires on-prem deployment or VPC-only access for production (affects procurement/legal).

I’ll attach a 1-page technical summary to share on Tue. Happy to run the short sandbox demo if helpful — 15 minutes shows the latency profile with a basic 1k qps replay.

— Rishi

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement

I reviewed the attached Sec questionnaire and flagged 8 items that typically require legal/engineering input from the customer side (data retention periods, subprocessor list, encryption key management, audit logs retention, SOC 2 report timeframe, incident response SLA, data deletion workflow, and egress controls).

Action items for us:
- Jordan: ask procurement if they can share their DPA template early — it will speed up redlines.
- Rishi: please confirm if audit logs can be exported to their SIEM (yes/no + format).
- Marissa: we should offer a SOC 2 readout window (we can commit to providing last 12 months of SOC 2 report under NDA).

I can draft suggested responses to all 8 flagged items by Wed EOD. If procurement wants us to pre-fill the questionnaire, we’ll need a short non-binding statement for legal.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Chu <aaron.chu@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finservco.com>, procurement@finservco.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap: stakeholder heatmap, procurement path & ally enablement

Thanks Jordan and team — appreciate the concise plan. I can do Tue 10/20 at 9:30am PT with Lena. A couple quick items for prep:

- Please send the 2-slide economic sketch and the SLA & DPA examples beforehand so Finance can scan.
- For the committed capacity options, provide a conservative ARR delta and comment on early-termination terms.

Lena — thanks for championing this internally. If you can share any internal notes you want emphasized to Finance, send them to me and I’ll include in the meeting.

Aaron Chu
Director, Finance Operations | FinServCo
